hook_line: I am not the kind of person who cries at lines on a page, except I do.
why: Opens with a direct identity contradiction that immediately creates tension, and resolves into a universal emotional admission about poetry finding unmapped nerves.

hook_line: Here is the thing about elegant code — programmers call it beautiful. They always have.
why: Unexpected bridge between technical and artistic identity lands the core thesis — code and poetry share the same curiosity — in under a minute, perfectly self-contained.

hook_line: The best scientific papers have rhythm. The best commit messages have grief in them sometimes.
why: Bold factual claim reframes the server room as a poetic space, then pivots to a sensory scene (toast, char, warm bread) that makes the abstract concrete.

hook_line: Poetry is not elevated experience. It's ordinary experience seen clearly for one second.
why: Punctures the 'poetry is for special moments' myth and then builds to the hypnotic 'particular blue of a Tuesday afternoon' payoff — high emotional density throughout.

hook_line: No one sits down to feel grief poetically. It arrives unannounced, in the wrong font.
why: Pattern interrupt on how grief actually works, building to the memorable contrast — facts tell you what happened, poetry tells you what stayed behind — that earns a strong payoff.

hook_line: The times poetry has landed hardest on me, I wasn't looking for it.
why: Relatable admission about distraction and accidental discovery reframes the whole trap of 'waiting to be inspired,' ending with the patient-and-sideways metaphor as a cliffhanger.

hook_line: The door doesn't need to be wide. A crack is enough.
why: Unexpected reframe after a long build — the no-lesson thesis lands as both a philosophical payoff and a quiet call to action, making it a complete standalone closer.
